text:
Rutger McGroarty has spent the fall riding the bus between Pittsburgh and the AHL, and three outlets this week wrote about how he's handling it, including The Hockey News with a headline quote: "They'll Eventually Go In."

That refers to the goals. He has none in six games this season, with 1.1 expected, and one assist, his first point of the season, on Nov 21 in Nashville. He's playing 12 minutes in a defensive role, and the on-ice numbers in that tiny sample are good: Pittsburgh takes 60% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about eight points better than without him.

He was the 14th pick in 2022 by Winnipeg, traded to the Penguins before he turned pro, after a big season at Michigan (52 points in 36 games). Forwards picked around him usually reach the NHL for good: 78 of 101 with four seasons reached 200 games.

NHL Edge has his skating near the bottom of the league, which is the knock. What to watch: whether the defensive role is a path to a full-time job.
